page: Microsoft Azure D32a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 server family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7452 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The dedicated CPU allocation operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 caches. This hardware configuration is paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

The instance includes 819 GB of local SSD storage, while lacking any integrated GPU accelerators. In benchmark evaluations, the D32a_v4 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. Its multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and compression capabilities generally align with the average tier. Notably, the server achieves a top-tier rating in the PassMark memory score, placing in the top 10%, which indicates efficient memory subsystem performance. However, large-scale LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing with a 70B model, fall into the weaker performance tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32a_v4 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose workloads that require a steady mix of compute, memory, and local storage without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The inclusion of a local SSD provides fast temporary storage, making it well-suited for relational databases, web serving, software compilation, and moderate-scale data processing tasks.
